title: Desktop Thick Client Testing Foundation
goal: Add a first desktop / thick-client assessment slice so AegisPT can assess enterprise application surfaces that are not purely web, API, or mobile.
scope: Implement a bounded desktop/thick-client assessment path for authorized Windows or Electron-style application artifacts and locally reachable helper services. The first slice covers: extracted config and secret review, updater and code-signing posture, local storage and log exposure, IPC/named-pipe or local-helper endpoint exposure where observable, embedded URL/API endpoint inventory, transport-security posture, and selected authorization/misconfiguration findings grounded in the OWASP Desktop App Security Top 10. Keep kernel drivers, memory-corruption exploit development, malware triage, and unrestricted host instrumentation out of scope.
generation_reason: The audit found no first-class desktop or thick-client assessment coverage in the repo, while many enterprise assessments still involve Windows desktop, Electron, or helper-client attack surfaces. OWASP Desktop App Security Top 10 provides enough structure for a bounded first slice.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Bounded desktop artifact and helper-surface assessment only. No exploit development, no unrestricted process injection, and no kernel or malware workflows in this slice.
notes: Focus on artifact-backed posture and observable local-service exposure first.
Do not imply complete desktop reversing or offensive binary analysis from this slice.
Canonical finding schema fields must remain unchanged.

success_criteria: A desktop/thick-client assessment path exists for authorized application artifacts.
The first slice surfaces evidence-backed findings for config, local storage, updater, transport, secret exposure, and selected local-service risks.
Findings can reference OWASP Desktop App Security Top 10 categories where the mapping is clear.
Tests cover unsupported artifacts, missing artifacts, and evidence-backed finding extraction.
No exploit-development or unrestricted instrumentation path is introduced.
must_not_touch: pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: Desktop assessment stays bounded and evidence-backed.
No exploit-development or unrestricted host instrumentation path is added.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with desktop/thick-client implementation and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with the desktop assessment baseline and remaining limits.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
